testedVersions: PowerShell 7.6.10; Pester 5.7.1; mocked ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.x cmdlet shapes
Linux CI Pester with mocked Exchange cmdlets; not a live Exchange Online execution
prerequisites: Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7.x with ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.0.0 or later installed separately by the administrator
An already connected Connect-ExchangeOnline session to the requested tenant with read-only Exchange roles; no credentials in request parameters
limits: Implemented with synthetic tests only; no live Exchange Online tenant or certified module version
Read-only cmdlets only; recipients and permissions outside the connected session's RBAC scope are invisible
No message, calendar or file contents, no mailbox folders and no transport-rule conditions or actions

producers.apiVersion: Microsoft Graph v1.0 usage report CSV
testedVersions: Synthetic CSV fixtures of the documented Graph v1.0 getMailboxUsageDetail column set (byte units)
prerequisites: Consultant upload of a report downloaded with Reports.Read.All and a Microsoft 365 reports role; tenant attested by the consultant
limits: File import through report profile m365.mailboxUsageDetail 1.0.0; not verified Graph connection evidence
Admin center MB exports and localized headers are rejected

permissions: Exchange Online read-only recipient role such as View-Only Recipients in the connected session
sections.refreshStrategy: Full comparable tenant snapshot; absence is inferred only from a later complete snapshot of the same fields
limits: Soft-deleted and inactive recipients are not requested
Aliases include every EmailAddresses entry (SMTP, X500, SIP, SPO); only SMTP entries become match keys
Microsoft 365 group mailboxes appear as generic recipients; group membership stays in Microsoft Graph

permissions: Exchange Online read-only recipient role such as View-Only Recipients in the connected session
sections.refreshStrategy: Full comparable tenant snapshot of user, shared, room and equipment mailboxes
limits: Inactive, soft-deleted and group mailboxes are not requested
mailboxOf links only user mailboxes to a user: ExternalDirectoryObjectId first, then an exact UPN, then an exact primary SMTP address; shared and resource mailboxes stay independent objects
Mailbox keys are Exchange object GUIDs, distinct from provisional usage-report UPN references

permissions: Exchange Online read-only recipient role such as View-Only Recipients in the connected session
endpoints: Get-EXOMailboxStatistics -UserPrincipalName <UPN> -Archive (only when the archive is active)
sections.refreshStrategy: One statistics call per mailbox (and per active archive); a full snapshot is Complete only when every call succeeded
limits: Sizes are parsed from the documented 'n (n bytes)' value and are left null when unreadable; they are never estimated
Archive sizes cover the primary archive only, not auto-expanding archive extensions or recoverable items detail
Cost grows with the number of mailboxes; very large tenants need a maintenance window
Mailbox statistics can lag behind live mailbox content

permissions: Exchange Online read-only recipient role such as View-Only Recipients in the connected session
sections.refreshStrategy: One permission read per mailbox; the trustee is resolved only against recipients observed in the same run
limits: Only explicit (non-inherited) Full Access, Send As and Send on Behalf grants are reported; Deny entries are never reported as grants and suppress the same trustee's grant; NT AUTHORITY\SELF and orphaned SIDs are ignored
A trustee that is not a unique observed recipient (for example a non-mail-enabled security group) is counted in a sanitized warning and never invented, so the section is Partial
Folder-level permissions, calendar delegates, application access policies and Microsoft 365 group ownership are not collected
An edge is evidence of an observed grant, not of effective access

permissions: Exchange Online read-only recipient role such as View-Only Recipients in the connected session
sections.refreshStrategy: Full comparable snapshot of distribution lists and mail-enabled security groups with direct members
limits: Only direct members are reported; nested groups are not expanded
Dynamic distribution groups and Microsoft 365 groups are out of scope for this section
Members without a readable Exchange GUID are counted in a sanitized warning, so the section is Partial

permissions: Exchange Online read-only configuration role such as View-Only Configuration in the connected session
sections.refreshStrategy: Full comparable tenant snapshot of accepted domains
limits: Optional scoping context; does not prove DNS, MX or domain ownership
Optional section: run it only when the engagement needs mail-domain scoping

permissions: Exchange Online read-only configuration role such as View-Only Configuration in the connected session
sections.refreshStrategy: Full comparable tenant snapshot of inbound and outbound connectors
limits: Optional scoping context; smart hosts, TLS settings, certificates and IP addresses are not collected
Does not prove mail flow works

permissions: Exchange Online read-only configuration role such as View-Only Configuration in the connected session
sections.refreshStrategy: Full comparable tenant snapshot of transport rule metadata
limits: Optional scoping context; rule conditions, actions, exceptions and comments are never collected
A rule name can itself be sensitive: review before sharing the package

permissions: Reports.Read.All (delegated or application) to download the report; delegated users also need a Microsoft 365 reports role
sections.refreshStrategy: Consultant-uploaded report snapshot observed at the report refresh date
limits: Not a tenant-wide exhaustive inventory; absence from a report never proves deletion
Concealed user names are not converted or guessed
Mailbox keys are provisional report UPN references, not Exchange GUIDs
